newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ministries agree on land liquidity plan--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan ministries agree on land liquidity plan--MOF.

text.p: Four government ministries and the Tokyo and Osaka prefectural governments on Tuesday formally approved a package of proposals to boost liquidity in Japan's real estate market, a Finance Ministry official said.
The package is expected to be adopted as a government plan on March 31. It was in line with a set of proposals disclosed by the Finance Ministry on Monday.
The Construction Ministry, the National Land Agency and the Justice Ministry joined the Finance Ministry in approving the package, the official said.
Under the package, the government plans to permit the securitisation through trust banks of collateralised land used for commercial purposes.
The government will also permit the establishment of special purpose companies in Japan to take over foreclosed property and to issue bonds. This measure will be fully implemented in 1998/99.
Credits backed by collateralised land will be securitised through trust banks and the securities can be sold to investors in small lots.
The Japanese government will review taxation systems involved in the securitisation later in consultation with the Finance Ministry's taxation bureau.
